name: Poly Network
rootCause: Poly Network is back. Almost two years after topping the leaderboard, this time the hacker got away with just $4.4M. How many more bridges will get rekt because of a handful of compromised keys?

descriptions.text: Poly Network is back. Almost two years after topping the leaderboard, this time the hacker got away with just $4.4M. How many more bridges will get rekt because of a handful of compromised keys?

The Poly Network, a cross-chain interoperability protocol, was attacked again. This attack affected 58 assets on 11 blockchains. According to SlowMist analysis, Poly Network hackers have profited over $10 million worth of mainstream assets. The attackers implanted a Trojan virus into the program compilation environment, allowing them to acquire the consensus keys of Poly Network’s Relay Chain. Subsequently, they utilized these keys to forge cross-chain transactions. The hackers implanted a Trojan horse code block during the program compilation process, obtaining and uploading consensus keys during program startup. They then employed these keys to sign…

The July 2023 Poly Network incident involved an attacker forging bridge messages across multiple chains by compromising the keys for its off-chain validators, resulting in $10.2M of actual losses despite the ability to mint far larger paper amounts. Off-chain consensus keys controlling Poly Network’s cross-chain bridge were compromised, allowing the attacker to sign forged state roots and cross-chain transfer messages. Existing contract logic relied on these keys, so it treated malicious unlock commands as valid.
